newsitem.title: INDIA: Battenfeld buys out India partner, floats new firm.
newsitem.headline: Battenfeld buys out India partner, floats new firm.

text.p: German plastic machinery maker Battenfeld group took over the Mafatlal Micro Machines Ltd by buying out Arvind Mafatlal group's shareholding in the company, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Tuesday.
Battenfeld, which previously had a 51 percent stake in the venture, will fully own the new company to be called Battenfeld India Ltd, the PTI said.
The news agency quoted the vice-chairman of the Mafatlal group as saying the takeover was proposed by the Indian partner as it wanted to concentrate on its core businesses.
Mafatlal had a 49 percent stake in the company.
Mafatlal Micro Machines Ltd recorded a turnover of 230 million rupees ($6.42 million) in 1995/96 (April-March).
The new company's managing director Dr Helmut Eschwey said the company did not expect any change in its turnover for 1996/97.
"The turnover in 1997/98 would be 380 million rupeees ($10.61 million) and will grow to 450 million ($12.57 million) in 1998/99, the agency quoted Eschwey as saying.
